description: ASTROZEESA is a solo initiative led by Zeenathan Salsabil, establishing Astrotonetics—a revolutionary discipline bridging astrophysics and optogenetics. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, this project creates a first-of-its-kind health monitoring software blueprint. By linking cosmic radiation flux and microgravity to real-time DNA damage, epigenetic shifts, and cellular stress, ASTROZEESA turns astronaut monitoring into a predictive shield for deep-space survival.
summary: ASTROZEESA introduces Astrotonetics, an interdisciplinary aerospace medicine framework developed entirely by an independent teen researcher deeply passionate about astronomy, who firmly believes that astrophysics and human biology are deeply complementary sciences. Rather than treating biology as an immutable fixture, Astrotonetics establishes biology as a downstream expression of physical laws.To overcome deep-space failure modes—specifically high-LET Galactic Cosmic Radiation (GCR), microgravity bone loss, and cephalad fluid shifts—we engineered a 4-tier closed-loop biocybernetic architecture. Pairing real-time GEANT4 and SANS modeling with pre-flight AAV/LNP delivery of light-gated optogenetic switches and bone-homing UCNPs, ASTROZEESA autonomously triggers sub-cellular DNA repair (RAD51/BRCA1), antioxidant defense (Nrf2/SOD2), osteogenesis (Runx2), and vascular tone regulation.   This project replaces bulky, passive mechanical countermeasures with an active, continuous 24/7 biological shield. It is vital because interplanetary exploration to Mars demands self-correcting physiological systems that safeguard crew health without ground-station oversight.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

ASTROZEESA introduces Astrotonetics, an autonomous, 4-tier closed-loop biocybernetic architecture that implements an interdisciplinary aerospace medicine framework regulating sub-cellular genetic expression and tissue-level physiology via real-time astrophysical telemetry and precision photonic actuation.

  • Tier 1 (Sensing): Continuous monitoring of external/cabin radiation flux and wearable biometric telemetry.
  • Tier 2 (Modeling): Accelerated GEANT4 Monte Carlo particle-transport and SANS simulation kernels running real-time damage probability calculations.
  • Tier 3 (Actuation): Lightweight wearable near-infrared (NIR) textile arrays that penetrate deep tissues to illuminate pre-provisioned upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) and light-gated optogenetic switches (e.g., RAD51/BRCA1 for DNA repair, Nrf2/SOD2 for antioxidant defense, Runx2 for osteogenesis, and vascular tone modulation).
  • Tier 4 (Verification): Intrinsic intracellular bioluminescent feedback loops for continuous, closed-loop safety optimization.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Replaces bulky, reactive mechanical hardware (such as Lower Body Negative Pressure suits and resistive exercise equipment) with a continuous, 24/7 biological shield.
  • Safeguards crew health against high-LET Galactic Cosmic Radiation (GCR), microgravity osteopenia, and cephalad fluid shifts ("chicken legs") without restricting operational crew mobility.
  • Operates autonomously as a digital flight surgeon, requiring zero ground-station oversight.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to fundamentally redefine human spaceflight survivability, enabling safe, long-duration deep-space transit and interplanetary exploration to Mars and beyond. Furthermore, its core technologies offer profound terrestrial dual-use applications—including protecting healthy peritumoral tissues during cancer radiotherapy, radiation-free orthopedic micro-fracture diagnostics, and non-invasive management of severe orthostatic hypotension.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Simulation & Physics Software: GEANT4 Monte Carlo particle transport simulation toolkit, particle spectrometers, and tissue-equivalent proportional counter models.
  • Genetic & Biomolecular Frameworks: Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV) vector design models, Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs), lanthanide-doped Upconversion Nanoparticles (UCNPs), and optogenetic transcriptional constructs (BphP1 / ArchT).
  • Hardware & Telematics Concepts: Wearable NIR micro-LED smart textile arrays, optical plethysmography, and bio-impedance spectroscopy sensors.
  • Reference Datasets: NASA Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) RAD, ISS Radiation Data, Open Science Data Repository (OSDR / GeneLab), Human Research Program (HRP) Evidence Reports, and Badhwar-O'Neill GCR Environment Models.

5. How is your project creative?

ASTROZEESA and Astrotonetics break away from the assumption that Earth-bound medical science can simply be transplanted into the cosmos. Traditional medical science was shaped entirely by Earth's unique physical parameters—its stable gravity, dense atmosphere, and protective magnetic shield. If Earth's physics were different, our medical science would be different.

In outer space, where the physical parameters change entirely (zero gravity and intense galactic cosmic radiation), Earth's passive, terrestrial medicine fails. Recognizing that biology is strictly downstream of physics, this project does not impose Earth-bound medical science onto space. Instead, as a teenage solo researcher building this entirely on my own, I sought to invent the brand-new medical science built specifically to operate according to the physical laws of space. By merging astrophysics and human biology, it transforms the human body into an active, self-correcting biological system governed by photons.

6. What factors did your team consider?

As a 19 year old solo researcher who conceptualized and developed this entire architecture completely on my own through ASTROZEESA ; key design, safety, and validation factors considered include:

  • Clinical Trial & Testing Roadmap: Recognizing that this framework requires rigorous multi-phase experimental validation—spanning GEANT4 voxel phantom simulations, microfluidic tissue testing under simulated microgravity and heavy-ion irradiation, and eventual in-situ spaceflight payload validation.
  • Safety & Homeostatic Control: Preventing the over-expression of repair proteins or prolonged vasodilation by integrating low-burden, infrared-shifted bioluminescent reporter feedback loops (Tier 4).
  • Tissue Penetration & Biocompatibility: Overcoming the optical opacity of dense cortical bone by utilizing the optical transparency window (700–1000 nm) paired with bone-homing bisphosphonate-functionalized UCNPs.
  • Planetary Stewardship: Balancing the pursuit of interstellar exploration with a profound respect for Earth, recognizing that engineering artificial biological shields in deep space only highlights how miraculous, irreplaceable, and finely tuned our home planet truly is.
